text:
toni: FYI ap-southeast1 rack-c shows a weird taint oscillation. Pods land, quickly get Evicted with node taint `egress-degraded=true` then the taint clears. Result: micro-inference pods churn and fragmentation spikes.
vikram: saw that. kube-scheduler reports a bunch of `0/10 nodes: 5 Insufficient networkBandwidth, 5 node(s) had taint that the pod didn't tolerate`. But network counters on the TOR are fine.
sam-k: our NIC firmware rollout yesterday added auto-policing that marks ports transiently degraded for 1-3s during buffer reclaim. That explains the short taints. Scheduler reacts and spreads pods to avoid risk, which kills packing.
toni: options: (1) rollback firmware on affected racks (risky), (2) make taint `egress-degraded` a soft constraint for pods with `inference.rw/pack=soft`, (3) increase warm-pool to smooth churn.
ops: warm-pool currently 1 in ap-southeast1. Bumping to 3 would cost ~12k/mo if kept steady.
vikram: I can flip scheduler plugin to treat taint tolerations with lower penalty for pods <1 GPU for the next 24h. That buys time while infra coordinates with vendor.
sam-k: also propose we add a short debounce on taint creation at node-agent side for `egress-degraded` <5s. Prevents flip-flop. PR incoming.
toni: go with (dev-scheduler tweak now) + (debounce PR). ops, bump warm-pool to 3 temporarily. Monitor p95 latency and eviction rate for 1h.
infra-bot: Incident check: no platform alerts. Firmware rollout ID fw-2026-03-18 applied to racks c,d,e at 01:12Z.
vikram: scheduler tweak deployed (canary nodes): 2/3 micro pods now pack on same rack. evict-rate dropped 78% in canary.
toni: good signal. Keep monitoring and coordinate rollback only if debounce fails. Thanks :thumbsup:
